findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1 confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` applies numeric cursor conversion to the audit endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"`, so an authorized optimized request with audit rows raises TypeError while building its cursor and existing datetime cursors are also passed back to the timestamp query as raw integers by `return cursor.value`.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — [P2 confidence 100] `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` uses Redis's default SUM aggregation, so replaying a child into its already-redirected parent adds the duplicate payload's end timestamp to its existing destination score and causes older replayed spans to survive eviction ahead of newer spans instead of preserving timestamp ordering.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — [P2 confidence 100] `if span_count > 1000 then` hardcodes the insertion limit while removal of the loader's count guard leaves `self.max_segment_spans = max_segment_spans` unused, so callers configuring a lower maximum receive oversized segments and callers configuring a higher maximum lose spans at 1000 regardless of their configured limit.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — [advisory P2 confidence 75] `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the segment root when at least 1000 children finish after it, leaving flushed children pointing to an absent segment span despite the stored root marker; the strongest rebuttal is that roots normally finish last, but asynchronous children outlive their parent and the model enforces no timestamp invariant or root exemption.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — [advisory P2 confidence 100] `def get_result(self, limit=100, cursor=None, count_hits=False, known_hits=None, max_hits=None):` duplicates BasePaginator's complete pagination algorithm in OptimizedCursorPaginator, forcing every future cursor-boundary fix into two places and leaving optimized callers unfixed when only the base is updated; the strongest rebuttal is its special negative-offset branch, but extracting only slice selection makes the duplicated hit counting, reverse-page adjustment, cursor construction, and post-filter blocks unnecessary.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — P1 confidence 100: Replacing SADD with `p.zadd(` while retaining `set_key = f"span-buf:s:{{{project_and_trace}}}:{parent_span_id}"` changes existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without conversion or versioning, so inserts into pre-deploy buffered segments and `p.zscan(key, cursor=cursor, count=self.segment_page_size)` at line 434 fail with WRONGTYPE after deployment, while old consumers and rollbacks reject newly created sorted sets with their SADD/SSCAN operations.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1 confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError on the datetime field selected by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, so an authorized optimized-pagination request with nonempty audit logs fails with an unhandled exception instead of returning its rows.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2 confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes a negative start directly to Django when advanced pagination receives cursor `0:-1:0`, raising the ORM's negative-indexing exception instead of rejecting the invalid cursor with a controlled client error.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` discards excess spans without returning the eviction count or recording a metric, leaving ingestion operators unable to distinguish complete segments from truncated ones once traffic exceeds 1000 spans; although intentional eviction enforces the requested cap, that rebuttal does not justify removing the previous over-limit logging and metrics without replacement.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — [P2 confidence=100] `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` introduces an unrelated audit-log API pagination feature and its shared-paginator behavior changes into a task limited to spans-buffer insertion and eviction, forcing audit-log consumers and all BasePaginator callers to absorb changes that have no dependency on or traceability to the stated requirement.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — [advisory P2 confidence 100] The updated fixtures use `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0` throughout and never exceed five spans per trace, so deleting `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` or reversing its eviction order leaves every changed test's assertions unchanged and gives maintainers no regression protection for oversized traces; the strongest rebuttal is that permutation tests exercise real Redis across insertion orders, but those permutations neither enter the new `span_count > 1000` branch nor distinguish oldest from newest spans.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — [P2 confidence 100] `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` uses Redis's default SUM aggregation, so replaying a child into its already-redirected parent adds the duplicate payload's end timestamp to its existing destination score and causes older replayed spans to survive eviction ahead of newer spans instead of preserving timestamp ordering.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that zunionstore with default SUM aggregation will add scores together when the same member exists in multiple sets. Looking at the diff, spans are stored with their end_timestamp_precise as the score (line 196-198 in buffer.py shows `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})`). When zunionstore merges sets, if the same payload exists in both sets, their scores (timestamps) will be summed rather than keeping the original timestamp. This corrupts the timestamp ordering used for eviction via zpopmin (line 63-64: `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`), which removes elements with the lowest scores. Summed timestamps would be artificially higher, causing those spans to survive eviction when they shouldn't based on their actual timestamps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — [P2 confidence 100] `if span_count > 1000 then` hardcodes the insertion limit while removal of the loader's count guard leaves `self.max_segment_spans = max_segment_spans` unused, so callers configuring a lower maximum receive oversized segments and callers configuring a higher maximum lose spans at 1000 regardless of their configured limit.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the Lua script hardcodes `span_count > 1000` for the zpopmin limit, while the Python code in buffer.py has `self.max_segment_spans = max_segment_spans` as a configurable parameter. The diff shows that the Python code removed the span count check (lines 446-452 were removed from buffer.py), but the Lua script now enforces a hardcoded 1000 limit. This creates a mismatch where the Python configuration is ignored and the Lua script always caps at 1000 spans regardless of what `max_segment_spans` is set to.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — [advisory P2 confidence 75] `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the segment root when at least 1000 children finish after it, leaving flushed children pointing to an absent segment span despite the stored root marker; the strongest rebuttal is that roots normally finish last, but asynchronous children outlive their parent and the model enforces no timestamp invariant or root exemption.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the Lua script. Looking at the diff, `zpopmin` removes the members with the lowest scores (earliest end_timestamp_precise values). Since spans are stored with their end_timestamp_precise as the score (seen in buffer.py: `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})`), and segment/root spans typically start first and may finish before all children complete, the root span could have an earlier end_timestamp and thus be evicted when the 1000 span limit is exceeded. The code at line 63 `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` removes the oldest-finishing spans without checking if they are root spans. The has_root_span marker is set separately but the actual root span payload could be evicted, causing data integrity issues when flushing.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912) duplicates nearly the entire get_result algorithm from BasePaginator, including hit counting, cursor construction, reverse-page adjustment, and post-filter logic. The diff shows this is a real code duplication concern - the only meaningful difference is the negative offset handling branch (lines 875-882). This is a legitimate maintainability/architecture concern about the new code, not a bug or hallucination. Future fixes to BasePaginator's pagination logic would need to be duplicated in OptimizedCursorPaginator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — P1 confidence 100: Replacing SADD with `p.zadd(` while retaining `set_key = f"span-buf:s:{{{project_and_trace}}}:{parent_span_id}"` changes existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without conversion or versioning, so inserts into pre-deploy buffered segments and `p.zscan(key, cursor=cursor, count=self.segment_page_size)` at line 434 fail with WRONGTYPE after deployment, while old consumers and rollbacks reject newly created sorted sets with their SADD/SSCAN operations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows Redis operations changing from set operations (SADD, SSCAN, SCARD, SUNIONSTORE) to sorted set operations (ZADD, ZSCAN, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE) in both buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The finding correctly identifies that this creates a data type incompatibility: existing Redis keys created before deployment will be sets, but the new code will try to use sorted set operations on them (ZSCAN, ZCARD), which will fail with WRONGTYPE errors. Similarly, during rollback, old code using SADD/SSCAN would fail on newly created sorted sets. This is a real deployment/migration issue with no versioning or conversion logic visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1 confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError on the datetime field selected by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, so an authorized optimized-pagination request with nonempty audit logs fails with an unhandled exception instead of returning its rows.

adjudication.rationale: The OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key method at line 840 calls math.floor/math.ceil on `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. When used by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint with `order_by='-datetime'`, the key would be 'datetime' which is a datetime field, not a numeric value. math.floor() and math.ceil() cannot operate on datetime objects and will raise TypeError. The DateTimePaginator that was previously used handles datetime fields properly, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` discards excess spans without returning the eviction count or recording a metric, leaving ingestion operators unable to distinguish complete segments from truncated ones once traffic exceeds 1000 spans; although intentional eviction enforces the requested cap, that rebuttal does not justify removing the previous over-limit logging and metrics without replacement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the Lua script adds `zpopmin` to evict spans when count exceeds 1000, but the previous Python code in buffer.py had explicit logging and metrics for when segments exceeded limits (lines 443-452 show `metrics.incr('spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded')` and `logger.error` being removed). The new Lua-side eviction silently discards spans without any equivalent observability. This is a legitimate concern about operational visibility - the finding correctly identifies that eviction now happens without metrics/logging, making it harder to detect truncated segments. This is an important architectural concern but not a bug since the eviction is intentional.

This is a legitimate scope/architecture concern about the PR structure.
